site: Sheep Pass Formation, Egan Range, east-central Nevada (Nevadaplano) vs North Horn Fm, central Utah
method: clumped isotope thermometry (temperature contrast between two sites) + lapse rate
notes: Abstract: Nevada summer T ~13 C cooler than central Utah after 1.2 C secular-cooling correction; elevation difference ~2.2-3.1 km, broadened to >=2 km with age and climate uncertainties. Value is relative to the central Utah site (described as relatively low paleoelevation), so absolute elevation is >= the difference. elev_m is midpoint of 2.2-3.1 (ours). Paper is EPSL, not GSA Bulletin. Age 68-76 Ma from Snell's 2013 Caltech Tectonics Observatory presentation; abstract states Late Cretaceous to Paleocene. Coordinates are the Sheep Pass type section as given by Lechler et al. 2013, not by Snell et al.

site: Sheep Pass Formation Member B, Egan Range, east-central Nevada
method: clumped isotope thermometry (MAAT contrast vs coastal reference) + lapse rate
notes: Abstract: Delta47 MAAT ~16-20 C for the Late Cretaceous-Eocene Sheep Pass basin vs ~20-25 C for the Eocene coastal northern Sierra Nevada gives paleoelevation <=2 km for the early Paleogene basin. Member B age 71.5-61 Ma and coordinates from the paper. Maximum only. Marked weak because the coastal reference is Eocene, not coeval with Member B, and because it conflicts with Snell et al. 2014 (>=2 km) for the same basin; the conflict is the central Nevadaplano debate.

site: Sevier orogenic belt catchment, inferred from Two Medicine-Judith River foreland transect, Montana
method: oxygen isotope paleohydrology (proximal-distal d18O gradient) -> hypsometric mean elevation
material_or_proxy: lake and soil carbonate, unionid shells, gar scales, crocodile teeth (d18O, d13C)
notes: Abstract: isotopic patterns 'suggest a hypsometric mean elevation of ~2.6 km within the Sevier orogenic belt'; no uncertainty stated in abstract. Abstract says only Late Cretaceous; 77.5-74.3 Ma is from the companion GSA 2007 abstract by the same authors (Foreman, Lohmann, Fricke, Rogers). Coordinates are an approximate point in the thrust belt west of the proximal transect end. Weak: d18O-based, no stated error; lo_m/hi_m set to the point value because no range is published.

site: Tropic Shale and Tununk Member of Mancos Shale, southern Utah
region: Western Interior Seaway western margin (Sevier foredeep)
notes: Marine shale of the Greenhorn transgression in the Sevier foredeep; age bracket is the Cenomanian-Turonian stage span (ICS) from the title, not a dated section. Abstract text not accessed beyond title. Coordinates approximate (Tropic/Kaiparowits area).

site: Desert Member (Blackhawk Fm) to lower Castlegate Sandstone, Book Cliffs, Utah
region: Western Interior Seaway western margin (Sevier foredeep)
notes: Classic shoreface parasequences of the Book Cliffs; age bracket is the full Campanian stage (ICS) from the title. Abstract not accessed. Coordinates approximate (Book Cliffs near Green River, Utah).

site: Lewis Shale, south-central Wyoming (Washakie and Great Divide basins)
material_or_proxy: deltaic, marginal marine through deep-water marine shale and sandstone
notes: Abstract: Maastrichtian Lewis Shale deposited during the final major transgression-regression of the Late Cretaceous epicontinental sea; biostratigraphic ages ~71-69 Ma. Deep-water facies were below sea level, so the datum is an upper bound for the basin floor and a level reference for the adjacent Laramide region. Coordinates approximate.

site: Bearpaw Formation, Rocky Mountain Foothills and southern Alberta Plains near Calgary
region: Western Interior Seaway / Canadian Cordilleran foreland
reference_short: Kurita H. & McIntyre D.J. 1994 GSC Open File
notes: Abstract: dinoflagellates date the Bearpaw as Late Campanian in plains and foothills; the maximum western extent of the Bearpaw Sea was in the Late Campanian. Numeric bracket is the full Campanian (ICS) because the abstract gives only 'Late Campanian'. Foothills localities put sea level at the eastern edge of the Canadian Cordilleran thrust belt. Coordinates approximate.

site: Nanaimo Group, eastern Vancouver Island and Gulf Islands, British Columbia
material_or_proxy: fluvial-deltaic, shoreline, lagoonal and marine siltstone/shale in four transgressive cycles
reference_short: Muller J.E. & Jeletzky J.A. 1970 GSC Paper
notes: Abstract: four transgressive cycles with deltaic and shoreline, shore-bar/lagoonal and fossiliferous marine facies. Abstract states only Upper Cretaceous, so the bracket is the full Late Cretaceous; stage-level ages not read. Coordinates approximate (Nanaimo).

site: Great Valley Group, Sacramento subbasin, northern California
material_or_proxy: forearc basin marine strata (borehole-based 4-D basin model)
reference_short: Orme D.A. & Graham S.A. 2018 GSA Spec Pap 540
notes: Abstract: 4-D model of Great Valley forearc deposition from Tithonian through Maastrichtian, >1200 boreholes; peak sedimentation Turonian-Coniacian. Window clipped to 100.5-66 Ma. Much of the fill is deep-water, so sea level is an upper bound for the basin floor and a level reference immediately west of the Sierra Nevada arc. Coordinates approximate.
